messages:
maria_support: Escalation incoming — customer reports break when using JSON mode strict. They set "response_format": "json" and json_mode.strict=true and now get 422 but the body is an HTML error page. They say this started after yesterday's rate-limit rollout. Repro below (key redacted): maria_support: ```bash curl -i -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "model":"redwood-1-3b", "input":"summarize...", "response_format":"json", "json_mode": {"strict": true} }' ``` maria_support: Response they got (truncated): ``` HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 X-Request-ID: 01HWZ9ABCD1234

Quota exceeded

Please upgrade

``` maria_support: Customer expects application/json but sees HTML; parsing fails server-side because strict=true enforces JSON output. They want urgent help or a workaround. sam_engineer: Thanks — can you paste the response headers exactly and the full X-Request-ID? Which region were they hitting and do they have a proxy/edge in front? My initial guess: an upstream returned an HTML error (quota/rate limit page) and our strict mode tried to parse it and surfaced 422. Also ask them to include their Accept header — some clients send Accept: */* which can trigger HTML from CDN. maria_support: Headers from customer (redacted): ``` HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8 Server: CDN-Edge X-Request-ID: 01HWZ9ABCD1234 Cache-Status: HIT ``` maria_support: They confirmed their client does not set Accept explicitly (defaults to */*). They said it started after the rate-limit changes rolled yesterday. sam_engineer: Ok — two actionable items: 1) short-term mitigation: ask them to set `Accept: application/json` or set `json_mode.strict=false` to avoid strict enforcement, 2) engineering follow-up: we should ensure any gateway/edge responses for API paths return application/json even for error pages (or at least avoid serving HTML). Can you try mitigation and see if it unblocks them? I'll collect gateway logs for X-Request-ID. kevin_billing: FYI — the request id shows a prior 429 in the trace earlier this morning for that account. It's possible the CDN served a cached HTML upgrade page when quota was hit. Could be billing/plan enforcement hitting the wrong path returning HTML. I'll verify the account state. maria_support: Customer tried setting Accept: application/json and the request now returns a JSON error object and the client is unblocked. They want a postmortem and to know why they started seeing HTML at all. ops_bot: Incident created: https://pager.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-789 (owner: sam_engineer) sam_engineer: Root-cause hypothesis: edge/cdn returned an HTML quota page for API host when the account hit a limit; our json_mode.strict assumes the runtime response is JSON and surfaces a parse error (422) instead of a clear quota error. Short-term: communicate mitigation above. Medium-term: infra should normalize error responses for API endpoints to `application/json` and ensure cache rules don't serve HTML upgrade pages for API hostnames. I'll own the follow-up with infra + billing. maria_support: Noted — I've given the customer the Accept header workaround and the temp toggle for strict mode; they've accepted. Please add a short postmortem once you have logs. :thumbsup: sam_engineer: Will do, pulling gateway logs now and will update the incident with timeline + remediation plan. kevin_billing: I'll audit the rate-limit rollout and confirm whether account-level enforcement inadvertently served upgrade pages to API hostnames. maria_support: Thanks all — closing the support loop with customer for now, will wait for your incident update.
